02 — Configuration Coverage Metrics
ⓘ
Total number of rows in the uploaded EBOM file, including all part types — Collectors, References, Bulk Matl, and all active parts. No filtering applied.
Dev / Logic
r.length — raw result set length after runComparison().
Includes pt_collector, pt_reference, pt_bulk overalls.
Not used as a denominator for any issue metric.
—
EBOM Line Items
All items in engineering BOM
ⓘ
Active EBOM items after excluding non-reconcilable items. Four categories are excluded: Part Type = COLLECTOR, REFERENCE, and BULK MATL (structural placeholders, not physical parts), and REMOVAL items (EBOM lines whose Description contains "REMOVAL" without an "INSTALL" or "INSTL" override, plus all their indenture descendants — these are instructions to remove previously-embodied parts, not parts to be built). This is the reconciliation scope used as the denominator for all issue and coverage metrics.
Dev / Logic
total − ptExcluded.
ptExcluded: results where overall ∈ {'pt_collector', 'pt_reference', 'pt_bulk', 'pt_removal'}.
pt_collector/reference/bulk driven by EBOM col Z (COL.ebom.partType, index 25).
pt_removal driven by buildEbomRemovalScope() — description substring match on "REMOVAL" (case-insensitive), with "INSTALL"/"INSTL" substring override. BFS-cascades to all indenture descendants.
—
Active Scope
Excludes Coll / Ref / Bulk Matl / Removal Items
▱   EBOM → MBOM RECONCILIATION   ▱
ⓘ
The percentage of active EBOM items reconciled to the MBOM as a direct line item — exact PN+NH match with quantity satisfied. The strict 1:1 audit-defensible reconciliation rate against the manufacturing plan.
Dev / Logic
Numerator: rFunnelScope.filter(x => x.ms === 'ok' || x.ms === 'flex_ok').length.
Denominator: funnelScopeTotal (active scope minus A/B collectors — matches funnel scope).
ms is the MBOM-leg status; independent of ABOM.
—
% EBOM Line-Items Directly Accounted For in MBOM
Strict PN+NH match in MBOM ÷ active scope
ⓘ
The percentage of active EBOM items accounted for in the MBOM via any reconciliation path — direct PN+NH match (Pass 1), EBOM PN acting as a Used On parent (Pass 2), or a reconciled indenture ancestor (Pass 3). The broader planning-intent coverage rate. The gap between this and the strict direct % represents legitimate manufacturing restructuring (kit grouping, phantom resolution, reparenting).

The gap between this metric and 100% is composed of:
• Missing in MBOM — items that failed every path
• EBOM-MBOM Part Qty Mismatch — Pass 1 identity hit but quantity short
• EBOM-MBOM SUB/AR Items Not Used — SUB/AR items that failed every path (acceptable absence by design)
See the corresponding KPI cards below for breakdown. A small residual may also occupy gap slots in edge-case datasets (cancelled MBOM WOs, A/B collectors).
Dev / Logic
Uses Set unions to avoid double-counting: union(direct, usedOn, parent).
direct: ms === 'ok' || 'flex_ok'. usedOn: msUsedOn === 'pn_as_usedon'. parent: ms === 'covered'.
Population: rFunnelScope (active scope minus A/B collectors). Denominator: funnelScopeTotal.
Gap = funnelScopeTotal − (numerator Set size) decomposes as: Missing in MBOM (ms === 'missing') + EBOM-MBOM Qty Mismatch (ms === 'qty_mismatch') + EBOM-MBOM SUB/AR Not Used (ms === 'flex_missing'). All collectors and PT-excluded items are removed structurally by the scope filter; cancelled MBOM WOs do not appear as 'wo_cancelled' rows because the Pass 2 cancelled gate produces 'n/a' on the used-on leg rather than a status.
Same methodology as the Traceability Funnel MBOM panel.
—
% EBOM Accounted For in MBOM (Any Path)
Direct + used-on + ancestor ÷ active scope
ⓘ
Count of EBOM items with an exact part number + next-higher match in the MBOM. The strictest reconciliation status against the manufacturing plan — design intent captured 1:1 into MBOM.
Dev / Logic
rFunnelScope.filter(x => x.ms === 'ok' || x.ms === 'flex_ok').
ms = 'ok' when: mbomMap key (pn||nh) found and mq >= eq.
Bar denominator: funnelScopeTotal (active scope minus A/B collectors).

EBOM Line-Items Directly Accounted For in MBOM
Exact PN+NH in MBOM, qty satisfied
└─ 0 from processed SME Adjudication Claims
ⓘ
EBOM items whose part number appears as a Used On (next-higher assembly) in the MBOM. The EBOM PN is acting as a parent assembly in the manufacturing plan structure — common when an EBOM-defined sub-assembly is itself used to organize child parts in the MBOM. Mirrors the ABOM-side "Embodied as Used On Parts" card, scoped to the MBOM.

Per-leg count vs. Traceability Funnel: this card uses a per-leg independent count — an item with BOTH a Pass 1 direct hit AND a Pass 2 Used-On hit is counted on BOTH the Direct card AND this card (two independent facts about one item). The Traceability Funnel's Used-On stage uses an additive "+ via this pass" semantic instead — it only counts items NOT already credited at Pass 1, so the funnel number will typically be lower. Both views are correct; they answer different questions ("how many items have this leg's evidence?" vs. "how many items does this pass newly account for?").
Dev / Logic
rFunnelScope.filter(x => x.msUsedOn === 'pn_as_usedon').
msUsedOn='pn_as_usedon' when EBOM PN appears as a Used On value in the MBOM file AND the WO status is not all-CANCELLED.
Per-leg, independent of ms.
Bar denominator: funnelScopeTotal (active scope minus A/B collectors).
—
EBOM Items Accounted For as Used On in MBOM
EBOM PN appears as Used On in MBOM
ⓘ
EBOM items reconciled to the MBOM through their indenture parent rather than as a direct line item — the part itself is not in the MBOM under its EBOM PN+NH key, but a reconciled ancestor part is. This captures kit-grouped and phantom-resolved items where the manufacturing plan tracks the parent assembly instead of the child detail. Mirrors the ABOM-side "Parent Indenture Embodied" card, scoped to the MBOM.

Per-leg count vs. Traceability Funnel: this card uses a per-leg independent count. An item that's both covered by an MBOM ancestor AND a direct Pass 1 hit in the MBOM is counted on both cards. The Traceability Funnel's Ancestor stage uses an additive "+ via this pass" semantic — items already credited at Pass 1 or Pass 2 are not double-counted, so the funnel number will typically be lower. Both views are correct; they answer different questions.
Dev / Logic
rFunnelScope.filter(x => x.ms === 'covered').
ms='covered' set by recursive ancestor walk during MBOM reconciliation when no direct or used-on match exists. Pass 3 ancestor must be in MBOM direct pool.
Bar denominator: funnelScopeTotal.

EBOM Items Accounted For via Parent Indenture Items in MBOM
Reconciled via ancestor in MBOM
└─ 0 from processed SME Adjudication Claims
ⓘ
EBOM items that are untraceable in the MBOM — failed every reconciliation path. No direct PN+NH match, not appearing as a Used On parent, and no reconciled ancestor in the indenture tree. These are the candidates for SME adjudication: real misses, non-physical EBOM artifacts (paper collectors, PMI annotations, rework/removal instructions), or items needing variance authorization.

Excluded by definition:
• SUB / AR items — when a SUB or AR (Part Qty Text) item fails all paths, ms='flex_missing' rather than 'missing'. SUB = manufacturer substitution at discretion; AR = as-required quantity. Absence is by design.
• REMOVAL items — EBOM lines whose Description contains "REMOVAL" (without "INSTALL"/"INSTL" override) and all their indenture descendants are excluded from active scope. These are removal instructions, not parts to be embodied.
Dev / Logic
rFunnelScope.filter(x => x.ms === 'missing').
ms='missing' when: not in direct pool, not in used-on pool, no parent ancestor, AND not isFlexKey.
An item with the nhMismatchMbom flag set (PN exists in MBOM under a different NH than EBOM specifies) but no other coverage will resolve here as 'missing'. The flag is orthogonal — it doesn't compete with cascade status — and is consumed by the EBOM-MBOM NH-Mismatch Adjudication Helper rather than by any standalone KPI.
SUB/AR items get ms='flex_missing' (not counted here). REMOVAL-scope items get overall='pt_removal' (excluded from rFunnelScope).
Shown/hidden based on getModeRequired().includes('mbom').
Bar denominator: funnelScopeTotal.

Untraceable — failed all reconciliation paths

└─ 0 covered by processed SME Adjudication Claims
ⓘ
Parts found in the MBOM but where the planned quantity is less than the EBOM-specified quantity. Indicates the manufacturing plan under-allocated this part relative to design intent.
Dev / Logic
rFunnelScope.filter(x => x.ms === 'qty_mismatch').
ms='qty_mismatch' when mbomMap key found and mq < eq.
Bar denominator: funnelScopeTotal.

EBOM-MBOM Part Qty Mismatch
Found but planned quantity is short
ⓘ
EBOM items with Part Qty Text = SUB or AR that failed every MBOM reconciliation path. SUB = manufacturer substitution at discretion; AR = as-required quantity. By design, these items are not required to appear in the MBOM, so their absence is acceptable rather than a defect. Echoed here from the Traceability Funnel for KPI visibility — the gap between "% EBOM Accounted For in MBOM (Any Path)" and 100% consists of Missing in MBOM + EBOM-MBOM Part Qty Mismatch + this card.
Dev / Logic
rFunnelScope.filter(x => x.ms === 'flex_missing').
ms='flex_missing' when isFlexKey (Part Qty Text = SUB or AR) AND item fails all three MBOM reconciliation paths.
Informational metric — these items are excluded from Missing in MBOM by design.
Bar denominator: funnelScopeTotal.
—
EBOM-MBOM SUB/AR Items Not Used
Informational — absence acceptable by design
ⓘ
EBOM items where the part number reconciles to the MBOM but the next-higher (parent) differs from the EBOM specification. Restructuring is normal and expected in EBOM → MBOM transformation; manufacturing engineering frequently re-parents parts for assembly sequencing. This standalone KPI is retired in the live dashboard — the same nhMismatchMbom flag is now surfaced by the EBOM-MBOM NH-Mismatch Adjudication Helper, which couples the observation with a candidate-list for missing-item adjudication. The card is hidden but kept in the DOM for back-compat with session imports.
Dev / Logic
rFunnelScope.filter(x => x.nhMismatchMbom).
nhMismatchMbom is an orthogonal observational flag set on each result row by an independent query against the raw MBOM dataset. It does NOT participate in the Pass 1 → Pass 2 → Pass 3 cascade and does NOT take a status slot. The flag fires when the bare EBOM PN exists in the MBOM under a different NH than this EBOM row specifies (Pass 1 strict PN+NH would fail).
Items can co-occur with any cascade outcome: a flagged item that's also Pass 2-saved appears in BOTH the EBOM Acting as Used On card AND would land here. A flagged item with no other coverage resolves to Missing in MBOM AND would land here.
Card visibility: hidden by default (display:none). The flag itself remains live and is consumed by computeNhMismatchCandidates('mbom').
—
EBOM-MBOM Part Parentage Delta
Informational — restructuring is normal
ⓘ
The count of distinct highest-level EBOM items whose entire indenture subtree is missing from the MBOM. For each item with ms='missing', the tool walks up the EBOM next-higher chain until it finds either a reconciled ancestor or the top of the tree — the highest missing item in that chain is the "apex". Resolving an apex assembly first is the most efficient path to closing multiple missing items at once, because once the apex lands in the MBOM, its descendants may reconcile via Pass 3 (ancestor indenture walk) without requiring individual line-item fixes.

An apex with zero descendants is a standalone missing detail part. An apex with many descendants represents an entire unplanned assembly.
Dev / Logic
Computed in computeResultsMeta() after reconciliation.
apexMissingMbom: Map<rowKey "pn||nh", apexPn> — for each result row where ms==='missing', walk up NH chain via pnToResult; keep climbing while ancestor.ms==='missing'; last missing ancestor = apex.
KPI count = new Set(apexMissingMbom.values()).size (distinct apex PNs).
.size = total missing rows (matches Missing in MBOM KPI exactly).
Walk depth capped at 20 to guard against malformed cycles.
Self is apex when no missing ancestor exists above it.
Does not alter ms, overall, or any reconciliation status.

Missing APEX Assemblies (MBOM)
Highest-level unreconciled items in MBOM
└─ 0 covered by processed SME Adjudication Claims
▰   EBOM → ABOM RECONCILIATION   ▰
ⓘ
The percentage of active EBOM line items traceable directly to a closed work order in the ABOM. This is the most conservative, audit-defensible build completion number — only exact PN+NH matches with a confirmed closed WO are counted. The headline metric for Physical Configuration Audit (PCA) closure.
Dev / Logic
Numerator: rFunnelScope items where as === 'ok' || 'flex_ok' (ok_m, per-leg).
Denominator: funnelScopeTotal — rActive minus A/B collectors (matches funnel scope).
Formula: Math.round(ok_m / funnelScopeTotal * 100) + '%'.
Closed-WO is enforced structurally: the ABOM pre-filter routes only closed-WO rows into abomMap, so 'ok'/'flex_ok' statuses are closed-WO by construction.
—
% EBOM Line-Items Directly Embodied
Exact PN+NH in ABOM, WO closed ÷ active scope
ⓘ
The percentage of active EBOM items confirmed in the as-built (ABOM) by any reconciliation pathway — direct line-item with closed WO (Pass 1), EBOM PN acting as a Used On parent in the ABOM with closed WO (Pass 2), or a reconciled indenture ancestor found in the ABOM direct pool with closed WO (Pass 3). All three paths require CLOSED work order status — items present in the ABOM under non-closed WOs are NOT counted toward this percentage and instead appear in the "Part WO Not Closed" and "Used-On WO Not Closed" KPIs in the ABOM-only tier below. The broad as-designed-to-as-built coverage rate, scoped to closed work orders.

The gap between this metric and 100% is composed of:
• Missing in ABOM — items that failed every path at any WO status
• EBOM-ABOM Part Qty Mismatch — Pass 1 identity hit but quantity short
• EBOM-ABOM SUB/AR Items Not Embodied — SUB/AR items that failed every path (acceptable absence by design)
• Part WO Not Closed / Used-On WO Not Closed — items present in ABOM under non-closed work orders
• Proc Code: Removed from Build — items present only as removal proc codes
See the corresponding KPI cards in the issue tier, ABOM-only tier, and SUB/AR card for the breakdown.
Dev / Logic
Numerator: Set-union over rFunnelScope using per-leg predicates:
• direct: as === 'ok' || as === 'flex_ok'
• used-on: asUsedOn === 'pn_as_usedon'
• ancestor: as === 'covered'
An item meeting multiple predicates counts once (Set-union, no double-counting). Identical methodology to the MBOM Any-Path card and to the Traceability Funnel's overall coverage figure.
All three predicates are closed-WO by construction: the ABOM pre-filter partitions raw rows into closed/open subsets; abomMap and abomUsedOnMap are built from the closed subset only. Open-WO items get 'wo_open' status and are excluded from this numerator (they appear in the WO Not Closed cards instead).
Denominator: funnelScopeTotal (active scope minus A/B collectors).
Formula: Math.round(numerator / funnelScopeTotal * 100) + '%'.
Gap decomposes as: missing + qty_mismatch + flex_missing + wo_open + proc_removed (per-leg counts on the ABOM leg).
Mirrors the MBOM \"% Accounted For (Any Path)\" headline card, scoped to the ABOM with WO-closed enforced.
—
% EBOM Embodied (Any Path)
Direct + used-on + ancestor ÷ active scope — all WO-closed
ⓘ
Count of EBOM items with an exact part number + next-higher match in the ABOM where the associated work order is confirmed CLOSED. The strictest reconciliation status.
Dev / Logic
rFunnelScope.filter(x => x.as === 'ok' || x.as === 'flex_ok').
as_ = 'ok' when: abomMap key found AND aq >= eq. Closed-WO is enforced structurally — abomMap IS the closed-WO-only subset (built from the closed partition); no separate woStatus check is performed in the cascade.
Bar denominator: funnelScopeTotal.

EBOM Line-Items Directly Embodied
Exact PN+NH match, WO closed
└─ 0 from processed SME Adjudication Claims
ⓘ
EBOM items whose part number appears as a Used On (next-higher assembly) in the ABOM with a CLOSED work order. The EBOM PN is acting as a parent assembly in the as-built structure — closed WO demonstrates physical embodiment.

Per-leg count vs. Traceability Funnel: this card uses a per-leg independent count — an item with BOTH a Pass 1 direct hit AND a Pass 2 Used-On hit is counted on BOTH the Direct card AND this card (two independent facts about one item). The Traceability Funnel's Used-On stage uses an additive "+ via this pass" semantic instead — it only counts items NOT already credited at Pass 1, so the funnel number will typically be lower. Both views are correct; they answer different questions ("how many items have this leg's evidence?" vs. "how many items does this pass newly account for?").
Dev / Logic
rFunnelScope.filter(x => x.asUsedOn === 'pn_as_usedon').
asUsedOn='pn_as_usedon' set in Pass 2 when EBOM PN appears as ABOM Used-On AND the parent's WO is CLOSED (the open-WO subset routes to asUsedOn='wo_open' instead, surfaced in the Used-On WO Not Closed card). Per-leg flag — independent of direct pool / other legs.
Bar denominator: funnelScopeTotal.
—
Embodied as Used On Parts
EBOM PN appears as Used On in ABOM, WO closed
ⓘ
EBOM items not directly present in the ABOM but covered because a reconciled ancestor part number was found in the ABOM direct pool with CLOSED work order via recursive indenture tree walk. WO-closed is required on the ancestor — the ancestor must satisfy Pass 1 (direct pool, WO closed) for the descendant to qualify for parent-indenture coverage. Pass 2 (used-on) ancestors do not qualify for this coverage by design. Items whose only ancestor in the ABOM has an open WO are not covered here.

Per-leg count vs. Traceability Funnel: this card uses a per-leg independent count. The Traceability Funnel's Ancestor stage uses an additive "+ via this pass" semantic — items already credited at Pass 1 or Pass 2 are not double-counted, so the funnel number will typically be lower. Both views are correct; they answer different questions.
Dev / Logic
rFunnelScope.filter(x => x.as === 'covered').
as='covered' set when item fails Pass 1 and Pass 2 in ABOM AND coveredByParentAbom === true.
coveredByParentAbom is set only when ancestor PN+NH is in abomMap direct pool with WO CLOSED (abomMap is closed-only by construction — built from the closed-WO partition).
Ancestor walk: PN → NH chain, maxDepth=10.
Bar denominator: funnelScopeTotal.

Parent Indenture Embodied
Reconciled ABOM ancestor found via indenture walk — WO closed required
└─ 0 from processed SME Adjudication Claims
ⓘ
EBOM items that are untraceable in the as-built (ABOM) — failed every reconciliation path at ANY work order status. No exact PN+NH match in the ABOM (open or closed WO), not appearing as a Used On parent (open or closed WO), and no reconciled ancestor in the indenture tree. This metric is WO-status-agnostic: it represents items literally absent from the ABOM, not items present under non-closed WOs. Items present in the ABOM with an open WO are NOT in this count — they appear in the "Part WO Not Closed" or "Used-On WO Not Closed" KPIs in the ABOM-only tier below. These are the candidates for SME adjudication: real misses, non-physical EBOM artifacts, or items needing variance authorization.

Excluded by definition:
• SUB / AR items — when a SUB or AR (Part Qty Text) item fails all paths, as='flex_missing' rather than 'missing'. SUB = manufacturer substitution at discretion; AR = as-required quantity. Absence is by design.
• REMOVAL items — EBOM lines whose Description contains "REMOVAL" (without "INSTALL"/"INSTL" override) and all their indenture descendants are excluded from active scope. These are removal instructions, not parts to be embodied.
Dev / Logic
rFunnelScope.filter(x => x.as === 'missing').
as='missing' is assigned by the cascade only when ALL of these fail:
• Pass 1 against closed-WO abomMap (no exact pn||nh match)
• Pass 2 against closed-WO abomUsedOnMap (CI/EBOM PN not a Used-On value)
• Pass 3 ancestor walk against closed-WO abomMap (no covered ancestor)
• Second-lookup against open-WO openAbomMap (no direct hit)
• Second-lookup against open-WO openAbomUsedOnMap (no used-on hit)
The open-subset second-lookup preserves WO-agnostic semantics — only items literally absent from raw ABOM resolve to 'missing'. Items present only on open WOs route to 'wo_open' instead.
An item with the nhMismatchAbom flag (PN exists in ABOM under a different NH than EBOM specifies) but no other coverage will resolve here as 'missing'. The flag is orthogonal — it doesn't compete with cascade status — and is consumed by the EBOM-ABOM NH-Mismatch Adjudication Helper.
SUB/AR items get as='flex_missing' (not counted here). REMOVAL-scope items get overall='pt_removal' (excluded from rFunnelScope).
Shown/hidden based on getModeRequired().includes('abom').
Bar denominator: funnelScopeTotal.

rFunnelScope.filter(x => x.as === 'qty_mismatch') (per-leg).
as_ = 'qty_mismatch' when abomMap key found AND aq < eq (ABOM net qty < EBOM qty). Qty aggregation runs on closed-WO records only, so this metric represents finalized shortfalls — not in-progress partial installs (those route to wo_open instead).
Only flags shortfalls — surplus ABOM qty is not flagged.
Bar denominator: funnelScopeTotal.

Computed in computeResultsMeta() after reconciliation.
apexMissingAbom: Map<rowKey "pn||nh", apexPn> — for each result row where as==='missing', walk up NH chain via pnToResult; keep climbing while ancestor.as==='missing'; last missing ancestor = apex.

Missing APEX Assemblies (ABOM)
Highest-level unreconciled items in ABOM
└─ 0 covered by processed SME Adjudication Claims
ⓘ
EBOM items whose ABOM records show a work order that is not in CLOSED status. Per-leg aggregate across both ABOM pools — direct-pool open WO (as='wo_open') OR used-on-pool open WO (asUsedOn='wo_open'). Items in here have a build that is in progress, on hold, or otherwise not yet finalized — they are not yet eligible to count as embodied.
Dev / Logic
rFunnelScope.filter(x => x.as === 'wo_open' || x.asUsedOn === 'wo_open') (per-leg union).
The 'wo_open' status is set by the second-lookup: when closed-WO Pass 1 / 2 / 3 all fail AND the open-WO subset contains the item. as='wo_open' indicates the direct-pool open-WO presence; asUsedOn='wo_open' indicates the used-on-pool open-WO presence. An item with both is counted once via Set membership.
Bar denominator: funnelScopeTotal.

Part WO Status: Not Closed
ABOM records show a non-closed WO (any pool)
ⓘ
EBOM items whose part number appears as an ABOM Used-On value, but the associated work order is not in CLOSED status. EBOM Traceability Funnel
↑ Click any stage or residual segment to filter the summary table · Click again to clear
EBOM Traceability Funnel — Plain English Guide
What is this chart?

This chart shows how many EBOM line items we can account for in the MBOM (manufacturing plan) and ABOM (as-built record), and which reconciliation mechanism found them. Each bar is cumulative — later stages include everything from earlier stages. The goal is to see how completely design intent flowed through to the build.

Reference bars (top, grey)

Total EBOM — every row in the EBOM file, including collectors, references, and bulk material.
Active Scope — the denominator for all metrics. Excludes Part Type = COLLECTOR, REFERENCE, BULK MATL, and any REMOVAL items (items whose description contains "REMOVAL" without an INSTALL override).

Coverage ladder (green bars)

Pass 1 · Direct — EBOM items whose exact Part Number + Next Higher combination appears in the MBOM/ABOM as a direct line item, with quantity satisfied and (for ABOM) a closed work order. This is the strictest, most audit-defensible reconciliation path.

Pass 2 · Used-On — cumulative: Pass 1 items plus any EBOM items whose Part Number appears as a Used-On (parent assembly) value in the MBOM/ABOM. The EBOM item is acting as a parent structure, not a child component. For ABOM, the associated work order must be closed.

Pass 3 · Ancestor — cumulative: all prior items plus any EBOM items covered because a direct-pool ancestor in the indenture tree was reconciled. Captures kit-grouped and phantom-resolved items where the manufacturing plan tracks the parent assembly rather than the individual detail part.

Delta labels (+N parts, +X%)

Each stage shows how many new items it contributed — items not already counted by a prior stage. This tells you which mechanism is doing the most work. A large Used-On delta means many EBOM items are being used as parent assemblies. A tiny Ancestor delta means the indenture structure is well-represented at the direct level.

Why funnel numbers differ from the KPI card counts

The funnel's Pass 2 and Pass 3 deltas show items first reconciled at that pass — items already credited at an earlier pass are not re-counted. The KPI cards for Used-On and Parent Indenture use a different semantic: they show items with any evidence on that leg, regardless of whether the item also has evidence on another leg. An item with both a Pass 1 direct hit and a Pass 2 Used-On hit is counted on the Direct card AND on the Used-On card (two independent per-leg facts), but only at the Direct stage in the funnel.

Both views are correct — they answer different questions. The funnel asks "how much did each successive pass add?" The KPI cards ask "how many items have this kind of evidence?" The headline percentages on the section cards use a Set-union (de-duplicated) calculation identical to the funnel's overall coverage, so the headline % and the funnel's overall % always tie, even when the individual card counts and funnel stage deltas don't.

Residual Risk block vs. Reference bars — the key distinction

Below the coverage ladder are two visually similar but conceptually different sets of bars. Reading them as the same thing is the most common source of "why don't these numbers match?" confusion, so it's worth being precise:

Residual Risk bars answer: "Of the items that failed every reconciliation pass, why did each one fail?" The population is the residual only — items not captured by Pass 1, Pass 2, or Pass 3. The segments are a mutually-exclusive decomposition: every residual item lands in exactly one segment, and the segments sum to the residual total.

Reference bars answer: "How many items carry this kind of evidence anywhere in the dataset, regardless of whether another pass already reconciled them?" The population is the full active scope. These tie to the section KPI cards exactly. They are not mutually exclusive — one item can appear on several reference bars — so they can sum to more than the residual.

Worked example — "Why does my KPI say 676 but the funnel residual says 641?"

Say the ABOM Part WO Status: Not Closed KPI card shows 676, but the funnel's WO Not Closed residual segment shows 641. Both are correct. Here's the gap:

The KPI card counts every EBOM item with any open-WO evidence on the ABOM leg — its PN sits on an open-WO direct line, OR its PN appears as a Used-On parent on an open WO. That's a per-leg population: 676 items touch an open WO somehow.

The residual segment counts only the items where that open WO is the sole reason the item didn't reconcile. If an item has an open-WO direct hit but also has a closed-WO Used-On save (Pass 2) or a covered closed-WO ancestor (Pass 3), then it did reconcile — through that other path — so it is not residual and is excluded from the 641.

The 35-item difference (676 − 641) is exactly the set of items that have open-WO evidence and a separate closed-WO path that already accounted for them. They show on the KPI card (they do have open-WO evidence) but not in the residual (they aren't actually blocked). To see the full 676, click the Reference WO Not Closed bar; to see just the 641 that are genuinely blocked, click the residual WO Not Closed segment.

The residual stacked bar decomposes items that the coverage ladder did not capture (failed all three passes). Segmented by reason:

🟥 Missing — not found anywhere in the MBOM/ABOM at any WO status.

🟧 WO Not Closed (ABOM only) — item is present in the ABOM but only via open work orders (direct pool or used-on pool), and no closed-WO pass saved it. Build is pending.

🟪 Proc Removed (ABOM only) — Pass 1 hit, but every record for the key is a removal/swap proc code. Item is traceably absent rather than untraceably missing.

🟨 Qty Mismatch (residual portion) — Pass 1 identity hit, qty short, no other pass saved it.

⬛ SUB/AR — Part Qty Text = SUB (substitute) or AR (as-required). Absence is by design; not defects.

▒ Other — edge cases that don't fit the categories above. Not click-filterable. Usually zero or very small.

Reference bars (below the residual block)

Reference bars show the full per-leg KPI populations from the section cards, for comparison alongside the residual decomposition. Each ties to its KPI card exactly and may exceed the matching residual segment (per the worked example above):

🟨 Part Qty Mismatch — total qty-short items. Includes both the residual-portion (in the residual bar above) and items that another pass saved.

🟧 Part WO Not Closed (ABOM only) — total open-WO items per the KPI. Exceeds the residual segment by the count of open-WO items that also have closed-WO pass evidence.

Click behavior: clicking a Reference bar filters the summary table to the full KPI population; clicking the corresponding residual segment filters to just the genuinely-blocked residual-portion. Comparing the two row counts is the fastest way to see how many of a given issue type are already covered by another path.

Between-panel delta badges (Δ Direct, Δ Final)

Shows how far MBOM reconciliation leads ABOM reconciliation, in percentage points. Neutral grey = MBOM leads ABOM (normal for an in-progress build — planning should be ahead of actuals). Red = ABOM exceeds MBOM, which is unusual and warrants investigation. Hover for exact per-panel percentages.

Click interactions

Click any stage bar or residual segment to filter the summary table to the items first captured at that stage — items not found by any earlier pass. Click the same stage again to clear the filter.

Coverage Curve (toggle)

The "Show Coverage Curve" button overlays a line connecting the right edges of each coverage bar. A steep early slope followed by flattening means Pass 1 is doing most of the work. A gradual slope throughout means you're relying heavily on later passes — consider investigating why direct reconciliation is low.

WO Status Roll-Up ▸ Rank non-closed WOs
ⓘ
Each bar shows the count of unique Work Order numbers from the ABOM file that carry that status. A single WO number may appear on many ABOM line items (one per part it covers), but is counted only once here. The status shown for each WO is taken from its first appearance in the ABOM file. When RFV data is loaded, non-Closed bars are split: the teal portion shows WOs with an RFV authorization; the remaining bar shows bare open WOs. A teal ◆ diamond marker with a count is drawn beside each non-Closed bar that has RFV-authorized WOs — teal color and the ◆ diamond both indicate RFV (Request For Variance) authorization.
Dev / Logic
Source: buildWoRollup(abomData, COL.abom.woNo, COL.abom.woStatus).
Deduplication: woMap[woNo] = status (first-occurrence-wins — subsequent rows for the same WO are ignored).
Total = Object.values(woMap).length — unique WO count, NOT ABOM row count.
RFV split: rfvWoCountByStatus built from abom woStatusMap × rfvWoSet (RFV Col E WO#s).
Canvas drawn by drawWoStatusRollup().
NCR by Cause Code
ⓘ
Each bar shows the count of NCR disposition entries matched to EBOM items, grouped by Cause Code. One NCR Number may have many Disposition rows — each disposition row is counted separately (not by unique NCR Number). Cancelled NCR entries are excluded. An entry that qualifies under both Pool 1 (discrepant part match) and Pool 2 (originating WO match) may be counted up to twice. Top 6 cause codes shown.
Dev / Logic
Source: ncrEntriesPool1.concat(ncrEntriesPool2) across all result rows — no deduplication between pools.
Filter: (ncrStatus || '').toUpperCase() !== 'CANCELLED'.
Groups by: causeCode + ': ' + causeCodeDesc (or 'UNSPECIFIED' when blank).
Pool 1 = matched via NCR discrepantPart; Pool 2 = matched via NCR originatingWo → ABOM usedOn.
Counts are entry-level, not NCR-number-level. To count by unique NCR#, dedup on ncrNum.
NCR Disposition Status
ⓘ
Each bar shows the count of NCR disposition entries (individual NCR file rows matched to EBOM items) grouped by Disposition Status. Like the Cause Code chart, this counts disposition entries — not unique NCR Numbers — and the same entry may appear in both Pool 1 and Pool 2. Entries with a blank Disposition Status are excluded. Cancelled NCRs are excluded.
Dev / Logic
Source: ncrEntriesPool1.concat(ncrEntriesPool2) across all result rows.
Filter: ncrStatus !== 'CANCELLED' AND dispStatus must be non-blank.
Groups by: dispStatus raw string (case-sensitive from source data).
Semantic colors: CLOSED=green (reconciled); WORKING/REVIEW/open states=yellow (attention); administrative states=neutral.
Top 6 statuses shown.

Candidates Helpers
⚑   SME ADJUDICATION CANDIDATES HELPER   ⚑
ⓘ
EBOM items with ms=missing that have at least one unclaimed MBOM record whose part number shares the same base as the EBOM PN but differs in dash suffix. A dash variant is an unclaimed MBOM PN matched against the EBOM PN directly (Pool 1), against an MBOM used-on value (Pool 2), or against an ancestor of the missing EBOM item walked up to 6 indenture levels (Pool 3). This does NOT change any reconciliation status — it is a separate investigative signal. A CSA SME should review this alongside the Missing in MBOM card. Phantom assembly nodes (EBOM intermediate design nodes not intended for physical build) typically generate no candidates and will not appear here. Items are grouped by EBOM anchor with cascade descendants listed beneath. Computed by Worker 2 after reconciliation completes.
Dev / Logic
Worker 2 (createNearMatchWorker) — runs after Worker 1 results posted.
Unclaimed MBOM rows: raw MBOM rows not in claimedDirect (inMbomDirectPool) or claimedUsedOn (inMbomUsedOnPool) sets reconstructed from state.results.
Candidate EBOM: results where ms === "missing" AND overall not pt_collector/pt_reference/pt_bulk.
Index: unclaimed MBOM rows are bucketed by base-PN (text before last dash, or whole PN if no dash) for both PN and Used-On fields.
Pool 1: EBOM PN base vs unclaimed MBOM PN base.
Pool 2: EBOM PN base vs unclaimed MBOM used-on base.
Pool 3: Walk 6 ancestor levels via ebomPnToNh; check each ancestor's base against unclaimed MBOM PN base index.
Match rule (similarityTier): three branches detect dash suffix variants — both-dashed/same-base, p1-dashed/p2-equals-base, p2-dashed/p1-equals-base. All use lastIndexOf('-') so multi-dash PNs resolve deterministically.
Cascade: walk nhToChildren from each anchor; flag missing descendants as cascade children.
KPI count = unique EBOM PNs with at least one dash-variant hit across any pool.

The ABOM represents the as-built reality — dash variants here suggest predecessor part numbers were installed under old work orders before the EBOM was updated. Computed independently from the MBOM dash-variant scan by Worker 2 after reconciliation completes.

These are candidates for SME adjudication as "embodied under alternate NH" — the part appears to be in the manufacturing plan, just under a different parent than design intended. Scoped by default to EBOM indenture levels C/D/E (configurable in the helper) since deep-indenture parts are typically procured embodied in their higher assemblies. Excludes MBOM rows already attributed as Pass 1 strict matches to other EBOM lines.

computeNhMismatchCandidates('mbom') — main-thread, runs at end of renderKpiBlocks().
For each result row with ms==='missing' AND nhMismatchMbom===true:

    p3_covered_ancestor — target PN was a Pass 3 covered ancestor for another row (softer)
    no_other — target PN has no other reconciliation attribution (medium)
Stored in _kpiData.nhMismatchCandidatesMbom.

These are NCRs the tool's automated trace logic could not anchor to any EBOM row — typically because the discrepant part column doesn't match any EBOM PN (data entry quality), or because the originating WO has no ABOM Used-On match. A CM SME may identify the correct EBOM line manually by reading the disposition text. CANCELLED NCRs are excluded. Source: computeUntracedNcrs() — called from renderKpiBlocks().
Build tracedSet from state.results: for each result row, scan ncrEntriesPool1 + ncrEntriesPool2 and add (ncrNum, dispNo) pairs to the set.
For each NCR row in state.boms.ncr.data:
  Skip if ncrStatus.toUpperCase() === 'CANCELLED'.

This view does NOT assert that the discrepant part is a Configuration Item. A CSA subject matter expert must review each entry to determine whether the discrepant part is acting as a CI in the context of that work order. Counts all dispositions regardless of status; CANCELLED NCRs are excluded.

ⓘ
The percentage of CI-scoped EBOM items that are directly matched in the ABOM as a line item with a CLOSED work order and quantity satisfied. This is the strictest, most audit-defensible CI reconciliation rate — a 1:1 CI PN + CI NH match in the as-built record with confirmed WO closure. Reflects CI-ABOM Pass 1 only.

Numerator: directReconciledCIs.length — CIs where result.as === 'ok' || 'flex_ok' (per-leg ABOM direct status).

Denominator: ciScopeCount (distinct CI ID + PN + NH combinations in CI file).
CI-ABOM Pass 1 only. Per-leg semantic — identical to the EBOM-ABOM section's "% EBOM Line-Items Directly Embodied" card, scoped to CIs.

% CI Line-Items Directly Embodied
Pass 1 direct match, WO closed ÷ CI scope
ⓘ
The percentage of CI-scoped EBOM items accounted for in the ABOM via any of the three closed-WO reconciliation paths — Pass 1 (direct PN+NH match, WO closed), Pass 2 (CI PN appears as Used On in ABOM, WO closed), or Pass 3 (reconciled ABOM ancestor found via EBOM indenture walk, WO closed). All three paths require a CLOSED work order. The gap between this metric and 100% decomposes into three issue-tier KPIs: CIs on non-closed work orders ("CIs — Open WOs"), CIs with quantity shortfalls ("CIs — ABOM Part Qty Mismatch"), and CIs absent from the ABOM entirely ("CIs Missing in ABOM"). Note: those buckets are not mutually exclusive — a single CI can appear in multiple buckets simultaneously (per-leg semantics), so their counts may sum to more than the gap.

Numerator: ciAnyPathKeys.size — Set union of directReconciledCIs + usedOnEmbodiedCIs + higherParentEmbodiedCIs, keyed by CI identity (ciId||pn||nh) to avoid double-counting.
Pass 1: result.as === 'ok'|'flex_ok'. Pass 2: result.asUsedOn === 'pn_as_usedon'. Pass 3: result.as === 'covered'.
All three checks use ABOM-specific leg status and all three require WO-closed.
Denominator: ciScopeCount.
Gap decomposition: ciOpenWoCIs (in ABOM, WO open) + ciQtyMismatchCIs (as==='qty_mismatch') + ciMissingAbomCIs (as==='missing'). Buckets overlap — a single CI can appear in multiple simultaneously (per-leg semantics).

The card is hidden but kept in the DOM for back-compat with session imports.
Dev / Logic
ciParentageCIs — CIs where result.nhMismatchAbom === true (orthogonal flag, not a status).
The flag fires when the bare CI PN exists in the raw ABOM under any NH that does not match the CI's stated NH. Detection is WO-status-agnostic — scans the full raw ABOM, independent of the closed/open partition.
Per-leg metric — co-occurs freely with any cascade outcome (a CI flagged here may also be Embodied, Open WO, Qty Mismatch, or Missing).
Card visibility: hidden by default. The drilldown renderer was retired; the flag itself remains live and is consumed by the EBOM-ABOM NH-Mismatch Adjudication Helper.
—
CIs — ABOM Part Parentage Delta
CI PN in ABOM under a different Next Higher
ⓘ
Count of CI-scoped EBOM items present in the ABOM via Pass 1 (direct line item) or Pass 2 (Used On assembly) but with the associated work order NOT in CLOSED status. The CI is physically traceable in the as-built record but the build is not yet complete or finalized. Per-leg metric — a CI with both a direct-pool open WO and a used-on-pool open WO appears here once. Pass 3 has no WO-open variant (it requires the ancestor to be in the ABOM direct pool with WO closed). Mirrors the aggregation of the EBOM-ABOM Section's "Part WO Status: Not Closed" and "Used-On WO Not Closed" KPIs, scoped to the CI population.
Dev / Logic
ciOpenWoCIs — CIs where result.as === 'wo_open' OR result.asUsedOn === 'wo_open' (ABOM-specific legs).
Deduplicated by CI identity (ciId + pn + nh).
'wo_open' status is assigned by the worker's second-lookup against the open-WO ABOM subset — items present in the open subset (Pass 1 or Pass 2) that failed the closed-WO cascade.
Complement of the "% CIs Embodied (Any Path)" KPI together with the missing and qty-mismatch counts: any-path-closed + open-WO + qty-mismatch + missing = CI scope (per-leg, may overlap).
Click to drill into the detail list.

CIs — Open WOs
In ABOM via Pass 1 or Pass 2 — WO not closed
—
CI Scope
Distinct CI ID + PN + NH combinations in CI file

CIs Missing from EBOM
CIs not matched in EBOM by PN + Next Higher PN
ⓘ
Count of CIs traced to one or more NCR dispositions whose Disposition Status is CLOSED. Uses the same two-path join logic as the open-disposition KPI. Path 1 (Discrepant Part Match): NCR Discrepant Part = CI Part Number AND the NCR Originating Work Order's ABOM Used-On value = CI Next Higher PN. Path 2 (Used-On Match): CI Part Number appears as an ABOM Used-On value for the NCR's Originating Work Order. CANCELLED NCRs are excluded from the population. A CI with both open and closed dispositions appears here AND in "CIs with Open NCR Dispositions" — the two KPIs are not mutually exclusive.
Dev / Logic
_kpiData.ncrClosedCIs — populated in renderKpiBlocks() from the NCR ↔ CI joiner.
Per (CI ID, CI PN, CI NH) row in the CI file, scan NCRs:
  Path 1: ncr.discrepantPart === ci.pn AND abomWoToUsedOns[ncr.origWo].has(ci.nh)
  Path 2: abomWoToUsedOns[ncr.origWo].has(ci.pn)
For each matching NCR, filter dispositions to those with Disposition Status = CLOSED.
CIs with at least one such disposition land in ncrClosedCIs[]. Each entry carries ncrEntries[] — the per-disposition records used in the drilldown.
Click to drill into the detail list grouped by CI with each disposition as a row.
—
CIs with Closed NCR Dispositions
CIs linked to NCR dispositions in CLOSED status
ⓘ
Count of CIs traced to one or more NCR dispositions whose Disposition Status is anything OTHER than CLOSED (i.e., still pending or in-process). Same two-path NCR ↔ CI join logic as the closed-disposition KPI. Path 1 (Discrepant Part Match): NCR Discrepant Part = CI Part Number AND the NCR Originating Work Order's ABOM Used-On value = CI Next Higher PN. Path 2 (Used-On Match): CI Part Number appears as an ABOM Used-On value for the NCR's Originating Work Order. CANCELLED NCRs are excluded. CIs in this KPI represent open quality items requiring SME attention before the audit chain can close.
Dev / Logic
_kpiData.ncrOpenCIs — populated in renderKpiBlocks() from the NCR ↔ CI joiner.
Same join logic as ncrClosedCIs but filters dispositions to those with a non-Closed, non-blank Disposition Status.
Each entry's ncrEntries[] carries the disposition records for the drilldown table.
Click to drill into the detail list grouped by CI with each disposition as a row.

CIs with Open NCR Dispositions
CIs linked to NCR dispositions not closed
ⓘ
The total count of unique CIs that have at least one RFV link via any of the three match passes — direct PN+NH (P1), NCR Disposition (P2), or Work Order (P3). A CI is counted once even if it appears in multiple passes. This is the broadest coverage metric.
Dev / Logic
Union of rfvP1CIs + rfvP2CIs + rfvP3CIs, deduplicated by CI identity key (ciId || pn). Computed in renderKpiBlocks() → rfvAnyCIs array.
—
CIs with Any RFV Coverage
CIs linked to at least one RFV via any pass
ⓘ
Counts CIs whose exact Part Number + Next Higher Part Number combination appears directly in the RFV file. Most precise form of variance authorization — written explicitly against that part in its assembly context.
Dev / Logic
For each CI row: look up pn + '||' + nh in rfvByPnNh map. Match is exact after normPN(). Computed in renderKpiBlocks() → rfvP1CIs array.
—
CIs with Direct RFV (P1)
CI PN+NH matched directly to RFV Part Number+NH
ⓘ
Counts CIs linked to an RFV through the work order chain via three geometries: A — CI PN+NH in ABOM as component; B — CI PN as next-higher assembly in ABOM; C — CI covered via indenture ancestor whose WO appears in the RFV file.
Dev / Logic
Three ABOM WO maps (abomKeyToWos / abomUoToWos / abomAncestorPnToWos). Each RFV entry tagged with geometry A/B/C for drill-down display. Computed in renderKpiBlocks() → rfvP3CIs array.
—
CIs with RFV via Work Order (P3)
CI has an ABOM WO# that appears in the RFV file
ⓘ
Counts CIs linked to an RFV through the quality chain: CI is connected to an NCR whose Disposition Number appears in the RFV file. Checks ALL NCR dispositions regardless of status. Requires the NCR file to be loaded.
Dev / Logic
Step 1 — CI → NCR join (all dispositions, not just open). Step 2 — NCR dispNo → RFV join via rfvByDispNo. Computed in renderKpiBlocks() → rfvP2CIs array. Dims if NCR file not loaded.

CIs with RFV via NCR Disp (P2)
CI linked to an NCR whose Disp# is covered by an RFV
◆   ACN TRACEABILITY   ◆
ⓘ
Counts how many CI rows have a matching Approval and Clearance Notice (ACN), out of all CI rows loaded. The join is: CI Part Number = ACN Part Number. Because ACNs are part-number-based while CIs are defined by a Part Number + Next Higher Part Number combination, a single ACN can authorize multiple CI rows. CI rows are therefore not deduplicated — each CI row is evaluated individually. Click to see which CIs trace to an ACN and which do not.
Dev / Logic
Source: renderAcnKpis() → ciAcnLinked / ciAcnUnlinked arrays.
Step 1 — Build acnByPn Map: normPN(ACN Part Number, Col C) → [{recNo, recRev, pn, level}].
Step 2 — For each CI row: normPN(CI PN) lookup in acnByPn.
  Hit → push to ciAcnLinked (row carries all matching ACN records).
  Miss → push to ciAcnUnlinked.
Numerator = ciAcnLinked.length · Denominator = total CI rows (no dedup by PN).
Stored in _kpiData.ciAcnLinked / _kpiData.ciAcnUnlinked.
—
CI — ACN Traceability
CIs traced to an Approval and Clearance Notice
ⓘ
Of all distinct ACN part numbers at Levels 4–7 (flight-eligible clearance range), counts how many are present in the ABOM with at least one net-positive installation proc code. A part is considered embodied only if at least one ABOM row carries an install-behavior proc code (any code not classified as remove or swap by the tool). Distinct ACN part numbers are used — if a PN appears multiple times in the ACN file, it is counted once. Click to see embodied and non-embodied Level 4–7 ACN parts.
Dev / Logic
Source: renderAcnKpis() → acnFlightEmbodied / acnFlightNotEmbodied arrays.
Step 1 — Build acnAbomAddPnSet: ABOM rows where getProcBehavior(procCode) === 'add'.
Step 2 — For each distinct ACN PN where level ∈ {4,5,6,7}:
  Hit in acnAbomAddPnSet → acnFlightEmbodied.
  Miss → acnFlightNotEmbodied.
Denominator = acnFlightEmbodied.length + acnFlightNotEmbodied.length (distinct PNs).
Stored in _kpiData.acnFlightEmbodied / _kpiData.acnFlightNotEmbodied.
—
Level 4–7 ACN Embodiment
Flight-eligible ACN parts present in ABOM build record
ⓘ
Counts distinct ACN part numbers at Level 6 (Interim Approval — customer authorization pending) that are currently embodied in the ABOM with at least one net-positive installation proc code. Level 6 means final customer authorization has not yet been granted. Parts embodied at this level may require follow-up to confirm authorization has been obtained. Click to see which Level 6 ACN parts are embodied and which are not.
Dev / Logic
Source: renderAcnKpis() → acnLevel6Embodied / acnLevel6NotEmbodied arrays.
Step 1 — Build acnAbomAddPnSet: ABOM rows where getProcBehavior(procCode) === 'add'.
Step 2 — For each distinct ACN PN where level === '6':
  Hit in acnAbomAddPnSet → acnLevel6Embodied.
  Miss → acnLevel6NotEmbodied.
Stored in _kpiData.acnLevel6Embodied / _kpiData.acnLevel6NotEmbodied.
—
Level 6 ACNs Embodied
Interim Approval parts present in ABOM — authorization pending
ⓘ
Counts distinct ACN part numbers that have at least one linked NCR with an open (non-Closed) disposition status. The join is: NCR Discrepant Part = ACN Part Number. An open disposition against a cleared part means a quality event is unresolved — this may affect the validity of the ACN clearance depending on the nature of the discrepancy. Click to see the ACN records and their associated open NCR dispositions.
Dev / Logic
Source: renderAcnKpis() → acnWithOpenNcr array.
Step 1 — Build acnNcrOpenMap: normPN(NCR Discrepant Part) → [NCR rows] where dispStatus ≠ 'CLOSED' and ≠ ''.
Step 2 — For each distinct ACN PN: lookup in acnNcrOpenMap.
  Hit (≥1 open disp) → acnWithOpenNcr.
Count = acnWithOpenNcr.length (distinct ACN PNs with ≥1 open NCR disp).
Stored in _kpiData.acnWithOpenNcr.
—
ACNs with Open NCR Dispositions
ACN part numbers linked to at least one unresolved NCR disposition
